title: "The post-election AI selloff: pricing a risk, not a law"
date: 2026-11-05
categories: [retrospective, policy, volatility]
---
::: {.callout-note title="Retrospective entry, written in hindsight" icon=false}
Written in November 2026, after the outcome was known, to practise the
journal's method on a past market day. The prediction is the one the
mechanism would have implied that evening. This entry is excluded from the
scored record, which begins with the entry of November 20, 2026.
:::

## Observation
<!-- REWRITE: yields fell and tech still collapsed. What does that rule out? -->

- SPY -4.41%, QQQ -6.49%: the worst day since April 2025.
- NVDA -9.26%, AMD -17.26%, SMH -11.2%. VIX +69.7% to 28.2.
- Safe assets rose: TLT +0.21%, GLD +0.81%. The 10-year yield fell to 4.84%.

## Mechanism
<!-- REWRITE: explain the difference between pricing a risk and pricing a law. -->

- Channel: cash flows and the risk premium.
- A Democratic sweep in the midterms raised fear of new rules on data-center building.
- Slower building would mean less revenue for chipmakers, so they were repriced.
- Yields fell, so the discount rate was not the cause.

## Prediction
<!-- REWRITE: this was close to a coin flip. What evidence would have justified more than 55%? -->

- 55% probability that QQQ closes higher on November 12 (five trading days) than $647.05.
- Reasoning: a policy scare is usually priced at its worst case on day one, before anyone knows what will actually pass.
- Wrong if QQQ closes at or below $647.05 on November 12.

## Scoring

- **Right.** QQQ +6.4%, SPY +3.3%.
- The link held: brokerages argued that extreme regulation was unlikely and buyers returned.
- Lesson: a probability near 50% was honest here. The outcome was good, but the evidence that evening was thin.
